messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: org=lyra corp (org_id=org_89f2) sustained QPS spike > 3x baseline, error rate on token-generation path trending up (429s from RL). Auto-mitigation triggered: org throttling applied (soft). See: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2243123456

Sara: paging oncall (maya) — lyra is hitting us across regions, initial reports show queued requests and client retries. Customer reported perceived slowdown in product.

Maya: on it, pulling logs. can someone handoff from the nightly rotation? I’m OOO after 11:30pt but available for this window.

Jonah: i’m here. looking at RL metrics — per-org buckets exhausted in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. token generation latency spiking to 800ms for the org. A bunch of requests are large-context (>8k) conversational streams.

Kevin: adding context: lyra recently flipped on the new summarize-on-write feature (beta). it fans out multiple calls per user action. likely amplification.

Sam: pinging account team — lyra is on a committed capacity plan but using more ephemeral jobs than anticipated. Sam->Lyra: please avoid mass backfills during the window.

Sara: immediate triage steps (from runbook): 1) Confirm customer impact (errors/latency) 2) Apply temporary org RL adjustment or targeted rule 3) Consider disabling risky feature server-side 4) Monitor fallthroughs + rollback plan.

Maya: confirmed customer error reports in support queue, ~120 incidents in last 10m. Severity: customer-visible latency and occasional 429s. We should do a short emergency RL tweak + disable summarize-on-write for their org as a stopgap.

Jonah: propose a two-step hotfix: A) reduce their burst window to 20s but raise sustained token rate by 25% B) add a feature-flag block for summarize-on-write for org_89f2 until traffic normalizes.

Kevin: agreed. prepared the commands. runbook-safe CLI:
```
# increase sustained rate, keep global safety checks
redwood-cli org set-rate --org org_89f2 --sustained 1.25x --burst-window 20s --reason "emergency spike mitigation 2243123456"

# flip feature flag off for summarize-on-write (immediate)
redwood-cli feature-flag set --org org_89f2 --flag summarize_on_write --value off --reason "emergency rollback"
```

Sara: execute when ready. take screenshots of API responses. tag this thread. notify security if we touch keys.

Jonah: applying RL change now. 

Jonah: (logs) response: 200 OK. rate config revision r-20260315-8 applied.

Kevin: rolling feature flag now.

Kevin: feature-flag API returned success. summarize-on-write disabled for org_89f2.

Maya: metrics starting to trend down for queue depth + 429s — latency moving toward baseline in us-west-2. Support queue mentions reduced. :thumbsup:

Sam: lyra PM confirms they temporarily paused a large ingestion job — they appreciate the flag rollback and will coordinate a controlled retry window.

Sara: followups: - add a temporary policy to prevent simultaneous mass backfills for orgs on committed plans (ops/pm action) - schedule a postmortem with lyra + oncall to discuss feature gating and traffic shaping - ensure telemetry retained for 30d for regression analysis

Maya: handing off to kevin for monitoring during the next hour. I will be reachable but stepping off primary rotation.

Kevin: acknowledged. keeping an eye; if we see re-escalation we'll revert the sustained bump and enforce stricter burst limits.

incident-bot: NOTE: mitigation actions recorded: rate-change=r-20260315-8, flag-change=ff-lyra-sumoff-20260315. Incident ticket created: INC-2243123456.

Sara: closing note: no customer data exposure, only traffic shaping and feature disable. schedule postmortem for 2026-03-16 09:00PT. thanks everyone.

Kevin: leaving this thread open for 60m then archiving.

Sam: adding a customer follow-up template to the incident ticket (ops -> account)

Maya: thanks team. great coordination. :heart:
